content.text:
I've submitted **index 25 (Mn 0.49 / Sr 0.51)** as the best composition. It gave a photocurrent of 4.26e-6 A.

The budget allowed only 3 photocurrent measurements, so I used them to sample three regions of the Mn–Sr line:

| Index | Mn / Sr | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.85 / 0.15 | 3e-8 |
| **25** | **0.49 / 0.51** | **4.26e-6** |
| 23 | 0.35 / 0.65 | 1e-8 |

The roughly 1:1 composition was about 100× higher than the other two. That ratio matches SrMnO₃, but I never confirmed it: I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so which phase is actually there is unverified.

It's also uncertain whether index 25 is the true best. With three points I only know the peak is somewhere between Mn 0.35 and 0.85. Nearby compositions I didn't measure (for example indices 22, 24, 20 or 17) could score higher.
